core_obligations: Note that the derived tensor product against the other ring is defined because the complex is bounded above (proof lines 16352-16355).
Choose the bounded complex of finite free modules witnessing pseudo-coherence, form the cone and record the acyclicity of the cone in the relevant degrees (proof lines 16355-16362).
Apply the derived tensor product to obtain a distinguished triangle over the new ring and use the vanishing statement to keep the acyclicity (proof lines 16362-16370).
Identify the base change of the bounded free complex with the ordinary tensor product and read off the required witness, then derive the pseudo-coherent case (proof lines 16370-16380).
proof_roadmap: Justify the derived tensor product (proof lines 16352-16355).
Take the witnessing map and its cone (proof lines 16355-16362).
Base change the triangle and keep the vanishing (proof lines 16362-16370).
Read off the witness and conclude (proof lines 16370-16382).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that pseudo-coherence at a degree survives the derived base change, and the proof is a 31-line argument that transports the witnessing map through the tensor product. It first notes that the derived tensor product is defined because the complex is bounded above, then chooses the bounded complex of finite free modules witnessing the pseudo-coherence, forms its cone and observes that the cone is acyclic above the given degree; exactness of the derived tensor product turns this into a distinguished triangle over the new ring, the vanishing statement for cones keeps the acyclicity, and since a bounded complex of free modules computes its own derived tensor product, the base changed map is the required witness. The two vanishings and the identification of the base changed free complex are the substance.
